note: The refusal and state names of the anchored certify form (evidence 2.1 links, RB9-F5 section 3). The Go constants (pkg/proof/v2/certify_names.go) are hand-written and checked against this file by a drift test (TestCertifyNamesMatchNamesJSON); the TypeScript constants (packages/verify/src/s3/certify-names.ts) are generated from it and tested against it. A refusal is rendered as name{field,field}: detail, fields in the order listed, integers in decimal and hashes as lower-case hex. index is the ordinal of the link in the document's links member for the four certify_link_* names that carry it (missing, start, end, invalid), and the position of the item in certify followed by check.hops for certify_item_without_effect. A detail is fixed text and never interpolated. Check order for each item of a sequence (certify, then check.hops) of an evidence 2.1 document, the first failing check names the refusal: (1) canonical form, no updates: an anchored item with no updates that is not the last of its sequence is certify_item_without_effect{index,block}, judged first; (2) the record's anchor is a Directory self-anchor (a plain refusal); (3) the anchor's minor block passes the previous one (a plain refusal); (4) the link is present (certify_link_missing{index}); (5) every step of the link is present (certify_link_invalid{index}); (6) the link starts at the previous verified root chain anchor (certify_link_start{index}); (7) the link ends at the item's root chain anchor (certify_link_end{index}); (8) the link validates (certify_link_invalid{index}); (9) the item's updates are proven and applied, an update the walk already applied is certify_update_replayed{txHash}; (10) the quorum; (11) no effect, the canonical form again: a non-final anchored item that applied no update (every update it carries is a transaction the walk does not apply, such as a write to an account other than the network or globals account) is certify_item_without_effect{index,block}, block being the item's own minor block. After both sequences, a link that no anchored item took (a surplus link) is certify_link_invalid{used}, used being the number of links taken, which is the ordinal of the first surplus link. A link that carries a member the receipt does not know (such as $epilogue) is certify_link_invalid{index}, unlike a record, whose unknown trailing field leaves the verdict unchanged.

names.name: certify_link_missing
names.detail: an anchored item has no link

names.name: certify_link_start
names.detail: the link does not start at the previous verified root chain anchor

names.name: certify_link_end
names.detail: the link does not end at the item's root chain anchor

names.name: certify_link_invalid
names.detail: the link is not a valid receipt of an anchored item

names.name: certify_link_unavailable
names.detail: no receipt links the previous root chain anchor into the item's root chain height

names.name: certify_update_replayed
names.detail: the update was already applied earlier in the walk

names.name: certify_item_without_effect
names.detail: an anchored item that is not the last of its sequence applies no update

names.name: certify_update_unproven
names.detail: the update's root chain position does not lie between the previous and this anchor's root chain index

names.name: certify_window_unaccounted
names.detail: the account's main chain holds writes the walk did not account for

names.name: certify_range_unavailable
names.detail: the Directory does not serve the minor-root range; retry

names.name: certificate_budget
names.detail: the certificate does not fit the transaction size limit (tx_too_large)

names.name: checkpoint_stale
names.detail: the evidence builds on a major block older than the newest verified one by more than the allowed lag
